slides.title: The nurse needs to obtain a sputum specimen from a client. What should the nurse
text: Question: The nurse needs to obtain a sputum specimen from a client. What should the nurse have the client do?
A. Apply sterile gloves.
B. Rinse the mouth with mouthwash prior to the collection.
C. Cough to bring up secretions.
D. Clear the throat.
Correct answer: C. Cough to bring up secretions.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Cough to bring up secretions.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Cough to bring up secretions.” – Deep cough brings lower-airway sputum
Not correct:
• “Apply sterile gloves.” – Clean technique generally sufficient
• “Rinse the mouth with mouthwash prior to the collection.” – May interfere with specimen quality
• “Clear the throat.” – Collects saliva or upper-airway secretions
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 8: “Take several deep breaths and deep cough”
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 8: “Early am, do not brush teeth, rinse mouth w/ water only, no mouthwash or toothpaste”

slides.title: A nurse notes that a client’s bed has a frayed cord that plugs into the outlet.
text: Question: A nurse notes that a client’s bed has a frayed cord that plugs into the outlet. Which of the following is the best response?
A. Plug the bed in to see if it’s still functional
B. Put a sign on the bed that says “do not use”, call engineering, and find a different bed
C. Ask engineering for electrical tape to cover the areas that are frayed, and then check to see if the bed is still functional.
D. Be sure it’s plugged into a grounded outlet only
Correct answer: B. Put a sign on the bed that says “do not use”, call engineering, and find a different bed
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Put a sign on the bed that says “do not use”, call engineering, and find a different bed
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Put a sign on the bed that says “do not use”, call engineering, and find a different bed” – Isolate and report defective equipment
Not correct:
• “Plug the bed in to see if it’s still functional” – Electrical shock risk
• “Ask engineering for electrical tape to cover the areas that are frayed, and then check …” – Improvised repairs are unsafe
• “Be sure it’s plugged into a grounded outlet only” – Grounding does not fix damaged wiring
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: The nurse is selecting dressings for a clean abdominal incision that will be allowed to heal by secondary intention. What principles should the nurse use in choosing this dressing?
A. Dressings should be simple as they will be changed at least every 4 hours.
B. The dressing should allow good air circulation through the wound.
C. Materials used in dressing this wound should keep the wound bed moist.
D. Absorbent material to wick exudates away and support drying should be used.
Correct answer: C. Materials used in dressing this wound should keep the wound bed moist.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Materials used in dressing this wound should keep the wound bed moist.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Materials used in dressing this wound should keep the wound bed moist.” – Moisture supports granulation
Not correct:
• “Dressings should be simple as they will be changed at least every 4 hours.” – Frequency depends on wound and dressing
• “The dressing should allow good air circulation through the wound.” – Open drying impairs healing
• “Absorbent material to wick exudates away and support drying should be used.” – Excess drying damages healing tissue
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: Which action by the client below demonstrates that the client knows how to properly ambulate with a cane?
A. The client holds the cane on the weak side and moves the cane and weak side forward together, and then moves the strong side.
B. The client holds the cane on the weak side and moves the cane forward, then moves the weak side, and then moves the strong side.
C. The patient should hold the cane on his or her stronger side and move the cane forward first, followed by the weaker leg and then the stronger leg.
D. The patient should hold the cane on his or her stronger side and move the cane and weaker leg forward at the same time.
Correct answer: C. The patient should hold the cane on his or her stronger side and move the cane forward first, followed by the weaker leg and then the stronger leg.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The patient should hold the cane on his or her stronger side and move the cane forward first, followed by the weaker leg and then the stronger leg.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The patient should hold the cane on his or her stronger side and move the cane forward …” – Correct strong-side placement and sequence
Not correct:
• “The client holds the cane on the weak side and moves the cane and weak side forward tog…” – Cane belongs on stronger side
• “The client holds the cane on the weak side and moves the cane forward, then moves the w…” – Cane belongs on stronger side
• “The patient should hold the cane on his or her stronger side and move the cane and weak…” – Can also be valid; source item ambiguous

slides.title: The nurse caring for a patient who is taking an adrenergic agent will expect whi
text: Question: The nurse caring for a patient who is taking an adrenergic agent will expect which side effects? (Select all that apply.)
A. Increase gastrointestinal motility
B. Bronchospasm
C. Dilated pupils
D. Vasodilation
E. Increased heart rate
Correct answers: C. Dilated pupils; E. Increased heart rate
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Dilated pupils
• Increased heart rate
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Dilated pupils” – Sympathetic pupillary dilation
• “Increased heart rate” – Beta1 stimulation increases rate
Not correct:
• “Increase gastrointestinal motility” – Sympathetic activity reduces motility
• “Bronchospasm” – Beta2 stimulation causes bronchodilation
• “Vasodilation” – Alpha stimulation causes vasoconstriction; some beds dilate
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 6 - Respiratory, slide 18: “Side Effects:  tachycardia, palpitations, HTN, dyspnea, HA, dilated pupils, anxiety, nervousness, GI upset”

slides.title: Legal issues related to medical records include which of the following? (Select
text: Question: Legal issues related to medical records include which of the following? (Select all that apply.)
A. Medical record entries can be altered or erased to increase accuracy.
B. The nurse cannot make corrections at all to the record.
C. The medical record is the legal documentation of care provided to a patient.
D. In the event of litigation, the medical record is often the only available evidence.
E. Medical record documentation should be based strictly on facts, not opinions.

Correct answers: C. The medical record is the legal documentation of care provided to a patient.; D. In the event of litigation, the medical record is often the only available evidence.; E. Medical record documentation should be based strictly on facts, not opinions.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• The medical record is the legal documentation of care provided to a patient.
• In the event of litigation, the medical record is often the only available evidence.
• Medical record documentation should be based strictly on facts, not opinions.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The medical record is the legal documentation of care provided to a patient.” – Legal record of care
• “In the event of litigation, the medical record is often the only available evidence.” – Important evidence in litigation
• “Medical record documentation should be based strictly on facts, not opinions.” – Objective documentation is essential
Not correct:
• “Medical record entries can be altered or erased to increase accuracy.” – Never erase original entries
• “The nurse cannot make corrections at all to the record.” – Corrections with audit trail are permitted

slides.title: The nurse administers bethanechol to a patient to treat urinary retention. After
text: Question: The nurse administers bethanechol to a patient to treat urinary retention. After 30 minutes, the patient voids 800 mL of urine and reports having a loose stool but no cramping or gastrointestinal pain. The patient’s blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. The nurse will perform which action?
A. Notify the provider of bethanechol adverse effects.
B. Record the urine output and the blood pressure and continue to monitor.
C. Suggest another dose of bethanechol to the provider.
D. Request an order for intravenous atropine sulfate.
Correct answer: B. Record the urine output and the blood pressure and continue to monitor.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Record the urine output and the blood pressure and continue to monitor.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Record the urine output and the blood pressure and continue to monitor.” – Document therapeutic response and monitor
Not correct:
• “Notify the provider of bethanechol adverse effects.” – No concerning adverse reaction established
• “Suggest another dose of bethanechol to the provider.” – Additional dose not indicated
• “Request an order for intravenous atropine sulfate.” – Reserved for severe cholinergic toxicity
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
